glosses: to throw out, to fling out, to hurl out
to chuck out, to kick out, to expel
разг. резким движением выбросить наружу, прочь
перен., разг. грубо прогнать, выгнать откуда-либо
перен., разг. уволить с работы, исключить или отчислить откуда-либо
Alternative form of throw-out.
Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see throw, out.
To discard; to dispense with something; to throw away.

examples.text: Just throw that pen out if it doesn't write anymore.
They decided to throw out the idea because it would have been too expensive.
I picked up Eminem and I liked it. He pretty much threw out today's standardized thug/club/dance and stack paper philosophy that a jabillion other rappers have already adapted.

The episode also opens with an inspired bit of business for Homer, who blithely refuses to acquiesce to an elderly neighbor’s utterly reasonable request that he help make the process of selling her house easier by wearing pants when he gallivants about in front of windows, throw out his impressive collection of rotting Jack-O-Lanterns from previous Halloweens and take out his garbage, as it’s attracting wildlife (cue moose and Northern Exposure theme song).

glosses: To dismiss or expel someone from any longer performing duty or attending somewhere.

examples.text: The board threw the man out, because he wouldn't cooperate and agree with their plans to remodernize the facility.
The ushers threw the woman out of the auditorium, because she kept shouting out insults to the guest of honor when he made his speech.

glosses: To offer an idea for consideration.

examples.text: Let me throw this out there – how about if we make the igloo out of butter? Would that work?
I throw out a challenge to the gay community to dare to walk into this dark corner and offer the light of brotherly love to help these people find themselves.

glosses: To produce in a haphazard fashion.

examples.text: This program keeps throwing out errors.

glosses: To emit.
To utter carelessly (a remark, suggestion, proposal, etc.).

examples.text: He threw out a couple of half-baked ideas.

glosses: To cause to project.

examples.text: Using the countless tons of rock from the cliff-face, supplemented by much more from inland, they threw out a huge breakwater, 2,000 ft. long and 80 ft. high, roughly at right angles to the quay, so forming an almost completely sheltered corner. Fifty years later, this massive mole is still standing up to the worst that the Irish Sea can do.

glosses: To put into a state of confusion.
To outdistance; to leave behind.
To cause or experience debilitating muscle or joint pain in (a body part).

examples.text: ...while he was putting on his coat, after having completed his work, in preparing to leave for home, he threw out his shoulder.
But why wasn't Mom there? Sick? No. Threw out her back carrying boxes of blood at a blood drive.

glosses: To throw out, throw away.
To kick out; to insult, complain or criticize

examples.text: I had rather she had flung out at me, as many a woman would do, than taken it as she did.

glosses: Lanzar, tirar, impeler o impulsar con fuerza algo, de modo que se mueva cierta distancia como consecuencia.

examples.text: El bravo general arrojó su sable a la otra orilla y gritó: "Va mi espada en prenda, voy por ella".

Se representa como una mujer desmembrada, ya que su hermano Huitzilopochtli arrojó su cabeza al cielo, pues ella, en complicidad con sus 400 hermanos, mató con su poderosa magia a su madre Coatlicue cuando ésta quedó embarazada de Huitzilopochtli de un modo deshonroso (por medio de una pluma).
Tuvo amores con la ninfa Pitis, a la que también pretendía Boreas, éste, movido por los celos, arrojó a Pitis desde lo alto de una roca.
